tagline: Across the hill towns, by way of a president's cheese.
intro: Route 116 starts in Adams, in the Hoosic River valley between the Taconic Range and the Hoosac Range, and crosses the hills east through Cheshire, Savoy, Plainfield, Ashfield and Conway to South Deerfield. Through Conway it winds.

Cheshire was the only Berkshire town to favor Jefferson in 1800, and when he won it made him a cheese. The pastor asked for milk from every cow in the congregation and allowed no Federal cow to contribute. The finished wheel was too heavy to trust to wheels, so it left town on a sleigh.

moments.title: Adams
moments.text: Quakers from Smithfield, Rhode Island, were among the town's first settlers, and the Quaker suffragist Susan B. Anthony was born here in 1820.

moments.title: Plainfield
moments.text: Five self-guided walks around this small town lead past cellar holes, mill foundations, tiny cemeteries and old apple orchards.

moments.title: Burkeville Covered Bridge
moments.text: Just south of Route 116 in Conway, this covered bridge of 1870 crosses the South River, built after a flood damaged the bridge before it.
